headline: Nine died at a church funeral. Jordan will hang three men.
summary: A court in Jordan sentenced three men to death by hanging on Sunday for the shooting at a church funeral in Karak on October 23. Nine people died and 34 were hurt. The men, two brothers and their brother-in-law, fled and were caught three days later in an abandoned house. Jordan had paused executions from 2017 until June.

cover_question.q: Why kill them for killing people?

cover_answer: That's Jordan's law. It had stopped using it until June.
table_question: Can a punishment be fair if it can never be undone?

5-7.script: Last month in Jordan, a country across the ocean, three men fired guns at a church where people had come for a funeral, and nine people died. Police caught all three in three days, hiding in an empty house. A court has now given them the biggest punishment there is. It happened a whole day away by plane, and the grown-ups have it.
5-7.why: Caught, in an empty house, in three days: the one fact a seven-year-old can hold onto.
5-7.why_long: A seven-year-old takes one vivid feature for the whole event, and here it is men with guns, so the script moves to the fact they can use: all three caught, in three days, in an empty house. Cantor found this age fears what could reach them, so the plane ride puts it out of reach. Expect "why did they do it?" Nobody knows.

8-12.chip: Bring it up if it fits the day
8-12.script: On October 23, three men shot at a church funeral in Karak, Jordan. Nine died, 34 were hurt. Police found them three days later in an empty house; they fired and were wounded. A court has sentenced them to hang, the top rung of Jordan's punishment ladder, unused from 2017 until June.
8-12.why: A ladder with a top rung is a scale they can argue about.
8-12.why_long: At nine a child is working out whether rules scale with the wrong, so the script hands them a ladder with a top rung and a fact that complicates it: Jordan left that rung unused for years, then climbed it. The chase to the empty house is the chain. Expect "did the police get hurt?" No. All three gunmen were.

13-17.script: Should a state kill the men who killed nine at a funeral? Jordan says yes: three sentenced to hang. Second: a week after the shooting, Jordan bombed a Syrian village and said it hit terrorists. Syria said five died, women and children among them. Can a country hit back across a border?
13-17.why: Two fairness calls, the gallows and the border, with facts for each.
13-17.why_long: A sixteen-year-old can hold two true things: the men killed nine, and a hanging cannot be undone. Kuhn showed argument is a practised skill, so the script adds a second case, the Syrian village, where the facts are disputed and they must pick whom to believe. Expect "what do you think?" Say it, then let them argue.

5-7.q: Why did they shoot people at a church?
5-7.a: Nobody knows yet. The police caught all three, and the families there are being looked after.

8-12.q: Why kill them for killing people?
8-12.a: That's Jordan's law for terrorism. It had paused executions until June.
Three days later, in an empty house. They shot at police and got hit.

13-17.q: Is the death penalty ever right?
13-17.a: Jordan paused it twice, the last from 2017 to June. Argue it.

13-17.q: Why bomb Syria for a shooting in Jordan?
13-17.a: Jordan says it hit terrorists. Syria says five villagers died.
